summary: Customer reports elevated tail latency after enabling adaptive quantization + prefix prefetch; requests per-tenant unwind/playbook
description:
Issue summary: BrightLane experienced a 95th-99th percentile tail latency increase (~2-3x) across a subset of production endpoints after enabling an 'adaptive' optimizer profile that toggles quantization and prefix KV-prefetch concurrently. Impact: customer-facing inference timeouts and elevated error budgets for two critical routes. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod-us-east), tenant BrightLane Analytics, model redwood-open-7b-q4_k_m, optimizer profile: adaptive-aug2026-v2.

Observed timeline: 2026-03-12 18:20 UTC - profile rolled out to tenant scope via console staged rollout; 2026-03-12 18:33 UTC - first spike in tail latency recorded; 2026-03-12 18:45 UTC - support alert triggered (automated SLO guardrail); 2026-03-13 - customer reached out requesting immediate mitigation and a safe unwind path.

Steps to reproduce (customer): 1) Call same production route with 100 concurrent warm clients using typical prompt mix (longer multi-turn conversations with prefix reuse). 2) Observe 95p/99p latency vs baseline. 3) Validate that disabling only quant profile returns median latencies to baseline but does not fully resolve tail spikes unless kv-prefetch is also reverted.

Observed behavior: tail latency increases primarily on sequences that reuse long KV caches and have heterogeneous prompt lengths; CPU-side queuing observed on the host that correlates with concurrent cache recomputation. Error symptoms: occasional 504 gateway timeouts, token generation stalls for 2-8s, higher retry rates from customer SDKs.

Expected behavior: adaptive profile should reduce p50/p90 token cost without degrading 95p/99p latency for this tenant workload.

Initial logs & pointers: - SLO alert: https://status.redwood-internal/alerts/alert-8892 - Console rollout snapshot: snap-2026-03-12-18:15 - Serving runtime logs (host-group 12-ux): /var/log/serving/host-12-ux/2026-03-12.log (see repeated "kv_cache_recompute" warnings) - Trace example: https://tracing.redwood/trace/0f3a9d - Observability dashboard: per-route latency: https://console.redwood/teams/brightlane/latency-dashboard

Customer ask: Provide a tenant-scoped unwind/rollback playbook that minimizes service disruption and avoids full pool-wide revert. Customer requests explicit steps, expected impact, and a staged validation plan they can follow with Support in a live window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's request pattern (multi-turn, 40-60 token completions, high KV cache reuse). 2) Apply adaptive-aug2026-v2 profile via tenant config. 3) Run sustained load generator (100 concurrent clients) for 10 minutes. 4) Observe p95/p99 and compare to baseline snapshot snap-2026-03-11-baseline.

investigation_notes:
Support: reproduced tail latency with customer's load pattern on staging clone. Hypothesis 1: adaptive-aug2026-v2 toggles both q-profile and aggressive kv-prefetch prefetching, leading to recompute storms when many concurrent long-sequence requests hit cache invalidation windows. Hypothesis 2: quantization path causes slightly higher per-token CPU deserialization cost for some kernels, which increases queuing under bursty multi-tenant scenarios. SRE found host-level queuing and dropped batches in logs.

Mitigations attempted: 1) Scoped rate-limit increase for tenant to reduce instantaneous concurrency (temporary relief). 2) Partial revert: disabling quant alone reduced median but not p99; disabling kv-prefetch alone reduced p99 by ~40%.

Proposed safe unwind plan (tenant-scoped, staged): 1) Snapshot current tenant optimizer settings (snap-id: tenant-brl-2026-03-12-18:10). 2) Stage A (non-disruptive): reduce kv-prefetch aggressiveness parameter from 0.9 -> 0.5 for tenant scope and observe p99 for 20m. 3) If p99 improves <20%, Stage B: revert kv-prefetch entirely to baseline and keep adaptive quant enabled. 4) If p99 still > baseline, Stage C: revert quant profile to baseline (roll to q-default-2026-02) using tenant config toggle. 5) Validation: run customer-provided load for 10m at each stage, check tracing, error-rate, queue-depth metrics. 6) Rollback safety: enable automatic short-circuit routing to a fallback model variant (redwood-open-7b-cpu-fallback) if token-generation stalls >3s for any request during rollback window.

Notes: avoid pool-wide rollback; use tenant-scoped config flags and controllers. Prefer staged deopt vs atomic revert to limit risk. Document expected impacts at each stage in the playbook and pre-agree with customer on acceptable SLOs during window.
resolution: Proposed workaround: staged tenant-scoped deactivation of kv-prefetch followed by quant profile revert if necessary. Support to schedule live window with BrightLane. No permanent fix applied yet; awaiting customer confirmation for staged window.
